unit.why: A first-person dream account from Megillat Setarim. On Rosh Hashana 5607 the author dreams of judgments against him, then of their sweetening, and a theft follows: a memorate with events, not a teaching.
unit.boundary_note: The closing heading 'שיחות קדושים ממה שנמצא בחיבוריו...' introduces the next section and is not part of the story.

stories.start_quote: עוד במגלת סתרים וזה"ל בליל א' דר"ה
stories.end_quote: ונגנב אח״כ סכין וכלי כסף עכ״ל
stories.summary_en: On the first night of Rosh Hashana 5607 the author dreams of harsh judgments against him and prays the next day with great joy. A verse about his death appears to him at the raising of the Torah, and on the second night he dreams that the Supreme Crown is revealed in mercy, with the Beit Yosef pleading for him. Only a theft remains decreed, and afterwards a knife and a silver vessel are indeed stolen.

quotes: חלמתי חלום ארוך שיש עלי דינים
ובליל שני חלמתי שנתגלה הכתר עליון ברחמים

tags.why: His Rosh Hashana prayer is depicted.
He prays in great joy despite the harsh judgment.

quotes: נתראה לי פסוק וראיתה אותה ונאספת אל עמיך
tags.why: A verse appears to him while awake, at the raising of the Torah.

quotes: שנתגלה הכתר עליון ברחמים ונמתק הדין
tags.why: A revelation of the Supreme Crown in mercy.
The theft left in the decree comes true.

quotes: והרב בית יוסף הי' מליץ טוב עלי
tags.why: The soul of the Beit Yosef acts as his advocate in the dream.

quotes: נתגלה הכתר עליון ברחמים ונמתק הדין
tags.why: The heavenly judgment, set in the upper worlds, is the dream's implied scene.
Kabbalistic terms: the Supreme Crown (Keter Elyon) and the sweetening of judgments.
A heavenly decree is averted, through self-sacrifice in prayer rather than by a tsaddik's intervention.
